players.notes: Radek was born in the Czech town of Vsetin in October 2003. His first club was Sigma Olomouc in his homeland, where he progressed through the junior ranks. The 6ft 6in goalkeeper’s form attracted attention across Europe, including England, where he moved to Manchester United in 2020. He quickly made an impact in Manchester, and by the 2021/22 season he was first choice for the Red Devils’ Under-18s, helping them win the FA Youth Cup and reach the quarter-finals of the UEFA Youth League. Radek progressed into Man United’s U21s and made his first appearance for the senior team in pre-season ahead of the 2023/24 season. He made his senior debut while on loan with Accrington Stanley later that campaign, making 18 appearances in League Two. After another pre-season with Man United’s first-team squad, Radek joined Austrian Bundesliga side Blau-Weiß Linz on loan for 2024/25. He kept a clean sheet on his debut and established himself as first-choice, making 26 league appearances. Another loan spell followed in 2025/26 as Radek made the move to Bristol City. It was a successful stint at Ashton Gate, with Radek being named the club’s Player of the Year and Players’ Player of the Year. He was nicknamed ‘The Wall’ by supporters and made 41 appearances for the Robins. Radek has been capped by Czech Republic at U15, U17, U19 and U20 level, and departed Man United on a permanent basis in August 2026 to continue his football journey at Boro.

Kyle was born in Chipping Barnet in September 2001 and joined Wigan Athletic’s Academy at the age of 13. The forward signed his first professional contract for the Tics in February 2019 and made his senior debut in October 2021. While there, he represented Scotland’s youth teams from Under-18 to U21 level. He scored his first goal for Wigan in December 2020 in a 1-0 win over Sunderland in Sky Bet League One. In the same month, Kyle scored his first senior hat-trick as Wigan defeated Burton Albion 4-3. The 2021/22 campaign saw the forward join Swansea City, but after making just two appearances for the Swans, he moved to League One Cheltenham Town on a season-long loan to gain more EFL experience. Kyle scored four goals before being recalled in January 2022, and the second half of the season saw him make 10 substitute appearances for Swansea. Another loan was on the cards for the 2022/23 season as Kyle joined Oxford United, where he scored 10 times in 41 appearances. His impressive form at the U’s earned him a permanent move to Blackpool. Kyle spent two years at Blackpool where he made 66 appearances, scoring nine times including a goal in the Emirates FA Cup against Nottingham Forest. In January 2025, Kyle made the move to Hull City. In his first full season with the club, he helped the Tigers get promoted to the Premier League, before he joined Boro in the summer of 2026.

Will was born in Welwyn Garden City in April 2005 before being raised in St Albans. The striker was initially in Arsenal’s Academy and joined Sheffield United in January 2021. It was in Yorkshire that he started to shine, with the 2021/22 campaign seeing scouts across the country take notice of his talents. Will captained the Blades’ Under-18s as they won the Professional Development League national title in an unbeaten season. He was the league’s top scorer. He scored 38 goals in 48 age group appearances for the Sheffield club during his time there. Spurs won the race for his signature in August 2022, and he scored twice on his debut for their U18s, before notching his first hat-trick two months later. The 2023/24 season was another big success for Will as he was named the Premier League 2 Player of the Season. He was Spurs’ top scorer, with 23, as they won the title. Will’s progress was rewarded with a senior debut in October 2024 as he started Spurs’ Europa League match against Ferencvaros. His first goal came in the same competition a month later, against Galatasaray, and another month followed before he made his Premier League debut. Will’s first taste of the Sky Bet Championship came in the second half of the 2024/25 season, when he made 11 appearances for West Bromwich Albion. He then joined Oxford United on loan for the entirety of 2025/26. Although Oxford were relegated, it was a season of huge strides forward for Will, who scored 11 times in the Championship. That saw him win Oxford’s Golden Boot, and he was also named their Young Player of the Year. With one-and-a-half years of Championship experience under his belt, Will made the move to Boro from Spurs in July 2026.

Sebastian was born in London before being raised in Columbus. The midfielder played for Hammarby's youth team between 2012 and 2013 while his father, Gregg Berhalter, managed the club. However, in 2014 he joined Columbus Crew, where he climbed through the Academy ranks. Sebastian was announced as a Homegrown Player in 2020 and got his first taste of MLS football against FC Cincinnati. It was a successful first season for the midfielder, who made nine appearances and helped his side lift the MLS Cup. The following season saw Sebastian join Austin FC on loan. He made his debut for the MLS side in a 3-1 victory over the Colorado Rapids and went on to make 18 appearances during the season. Sebastian was traded to Vancouver Whitecaps FC in February 2022 and made 18 appearances in his first season. The following campaign, he took another step forward in his development by scoring his first MLS goal in a 6-2 win over Houston. The 2023 season also saw the Whitecaps win the Canadian Championship for the second consecutive year. Sebastian made it three Canadian Championships in a row in 2024, while also registering two goals and four assists in MLS as the Whitecaps reached the MLS Cup play-offs. The 2025 season was a standout campaign for Sebastian, as he scored four goals and provided 10 assists. Vancouver reached the MLS Cup final but were beaten 3-1 by Inter Miami. This season, Sebastian has scored six goals and provided four assists in 14 MLS appearances. On the international stage, he made his debut for the United States at the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup. His first goal for the USMNT came in a 5-1 win over Uruguay, a match in which he also recorded an assist. After impressing for Vancouver, Mauricio Pochettino selected him as part of his 26-man squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The midfielder featured in every game for the USMNT during the tournament on home soil, scoring and assisting in their final group stage match against Turkey. With plenty of experience under his belt, the 25-year-old now makes the move to Teesside.

Max was born in the city of Fresno, California, in April 2001. After starting playing football aged five, he spent much of his youth days with California Odyssey Soccer Club, where he spent nine years. He attended San Joaquin Memorial High School, where he was named the league’s MVP for two years in a row.  At that stage, Max played as a forward, and his final season with that team saw him score 50 goals and provide 20 assists . He attended the University California, Davis, after being offered a full-ride scholarship as a junior. He led his team to a Big West Championship in his first year and was named the Big West’s Offensive Player of the Year in his second, despite missing five months with a broken foot. Max decided to leave college and play professionally ahead of the 2022 season, when he signed a contract with MLS Next Pro side San Jose Earthquakes II. After one season there, he was included in the 2023 MLS SuperDraft, and became the first player to be drafted out of MLS NEXT Pro when he was selected by Columbus Crew. Max excelled as a wing-back across two-and-a-half seasons with the Crew, winning the MLS Cup in 2023 and Leagues Cup in 2024. He was called up by the USA senior squad for the first time in January 2025 and made his debut against Venezuela. He was a regular for his country in the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup as the Americans finished as runners-up. Max has since gone on to appear more than 20 times for his country, including at the 2026 World Cup on home soil, as the USA reached the last 16. He was selected to play for MLS All-Stars in the 2025 and 2026 MLS All-Star Games before making the move to Boro in August 2026.

Fin was born in Kingston upon Thames and is a product of Chelsea’s Academy, having joined the London club at an early age. He demonstrated his versatility while with Chelsea, mainly playing as a centre-back but also performing well at left-back and in holding midfield. Fin's departure from Chelsea at the age of 16 prompted a move to Aston Villa, where he developed into an eye-catching, ball-playing full-back, but also continued to excel in other positions, too. He signed his first professional contract with Villa in July 2022, with another deal following in April 2024. By that time, he had firmly established himself with the club. He was a regular in the U18 Premier League in 2021/22, also playing six times for the U21s in PL2. He had seven goal involvements in 17 appearances in all competitions the following season, before 2023/24 saw him become a mainstay in PL2. Fin was now also beginning to make his mark at first-team level. He was an unused substitute against former club Chelsea in the Emirates FA Cup in January 2024, and his debut came four months later, when he was brought on against Olympiacos in the semi-final of the UEFA Europa Conference League. Fin made his first appearance in the Premier League in May 2024, coming on as a substitute away to Crystal Palace. The left-sider – who is a cousin of Arsenal and England midfielder Declan Rice – signed for Spanish club Real Union on a season-long loan in August 2024. The move saw him play regularly in the third-flight of Spanish football, making 27 appearances. Fin moved on loan to Swindon Town in League Two in July 2025, and went on to have an outstanding first half of the season. Swindon occupy a promotion position just beyond the midway point, with Finley’s appearances playing a key part in that. He played 23 times for the Robins in the league, scoring twice and assisting seven more goals, while he also registered two assists in the EFL Trophy. His appearances were mainly at left-back and on the left of midfield. He made the move to Boro in January 2026.
